power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

table.description:
Satya — Felt Intelligence: pre-registered reads
Raydyn, Inc., a Delaware public benefit corporation · satya.org · submitted for OSF registration 5 Nov 2026

WHAT THIS IS
Satya is an attention-continuity interface built on Felt Intelligence (FI). A person hears one dated line about their own past — the first reflection — and answers "That's me" or "Not quite"; their answer outranks the reading. Every count is published at satya.org/research with its date and denominator, misses beside hits. No outcome is promised; nothing here is called proven. Not wellness, not therapy.

DATA SOURCE AND LIMITS
Sessions on enter.satya.org and in the Satya app, 25 May 2026 onward, joined by the person's account id (uid); the person's own taps and own words; states graded to a fourteen-state ladder plus the Witness by fixed word lists. External series: English-Wikipedia pageview shares (War, Peace), weekly.

RULES THAT APPLY TO EVERY READ
- Exclusions: staff and test accounts (by a uid list held on file), sessions ending in technical failure, sessions under 10 seconds, and the founder's own rows. The founder is a participant in his own data; his uid is excluded from every count, and the number of excluded rows is published with each read.
- No person's words are reproduced in any publication.
- Who reads: one named person, Abhishek Kumar Raysingh, read-only, and no read before the read date. Each read publishes the analysis file used and its SHA-256; analysis files are frozen in this OSF project before the read they serve.
- Word lists: the word-to-rung lexicon of the tap path is frozen in this project as word_rung_lexicon_2026-11-05.txt, SHA-256 3414eb3116fcb953538cf9686be061c99efdc5903cce19c66dac0de27ccc804e. The transcript grader's state word lists are a second list; their fingerprint is added to this project before the first read that uses them (30 Nov 2026).
- Every read is published pass, fail, not yet decisive, or "not enough people yet", with both rates and both n, at satya.org/research.

PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN TESTS (first published on satya.org 17–18 Oct 2026; quoted here)

H4 · written 17 Oct 2026 before the data (satya.org/research): across weekly bins 25 May → 29 Nov 2026, does the weekly share of our people's state-namings below the Witness co-move with the weekly English-Wikipedia War share? Pass if Spearman ρ ≥ 0.30 (two-sided p < 0.05, 10,000 permutations); secondary, Peace ρ ≤ −0.30. Readable only if at least 25 weeks each have at least 15 namings. At the pace as of 17 Oct 2026 — about 6 namings a week — the 30 Nov read will probably say not enough people yet; it will be published as that. A pass is moving together, never cause. Whether a rise inside moves the outside is deferred until 10,000 members name a state. Fingerprint of the written test (SHA-256): c177e7defcd464624071bb2f357531f7095967a453b6659b7c9618874ad652d9

H5 · written 18 Oct 2026, before the data (satya.org/research-awareness): Does the pause mean anything? Among people whose first "That's me" is timed, do those who answered after 8 seconds or more come back for another session within 14 days at a rate at least 10 points higher than those who answered in under 2 seconds? Fisher exact, two-sided, p < 0.05. Readable only with at least 150 people and at least 30 in the fast group — as of 18 Oct 2026, 28 fast taps of 191 timed first taps the 30 Nov read will probably say "not enough people yet". A pass would be co-movement, never cause. The clock is unchanged: it still includes hearing the truth. Fingerprint (SHA-256): c3ca7163b0d4c428582ef7e44f2e41a3a7dc9e28676f51cec2138126bacb6adc

H6 · written 18 Oct 2026, before the data (satya.org/research-dimensions): Is it the state, or only the long session? Among sessions of 5 minutes or more — so length cannot do the work — do people who named a state return within 30 days at least 10 points more often than people in sessions of the same length who did not? Fisher exact, two-sided, p < 0.05; readable only with at least 60 named and 200 not named. Second, frozen now: among people who say what weighs most, does Restless name relationships at least 15 points more often than every other named state combined (at least 30 Restless people)? First read 30 Nov 2026. A pass would be co-movement, never cause. Fingerprint (SHA-256): 069ac770c82f15adcc6a2e8ef46828ed37d391373505183ddbb8da2b128d06c4

NEW TESTS, WRITTEN AND SUBMITTED TODAY (5 Nov 2026), BEFORE EITHER READ DATE

H7 (5 Nov 2026): the shuffled read

Question. Does a person say "That's me" to their own first reflection more often than to a first reflection written for a stranger?

Window. Opens at the first 00:00 UTC after the shuffled-delivery build is live in all three markets (US, UK, India). That date is published at satya.org/research before the first tap counts. The window stays open until readability is met.

Consent. Before the tap every person sees: "The line you are about to hear was written either for you or for someone else. Tell us if it's you. Your own line follows either way." The shuffled line carries no name, birth data or place. A person who declines goes straight to their own reflection, is excluded from both arms, and is counted.

Conditions. At generation, each person is randomly assigned 1:1. True read: the first reflection generated for person X is delivered to X. Shuffled read: the first reflection generated for X is delivered, unaltered, to person Y — same market, same language — and Y scores it with the same tap. Y receives their own reflection immediately after tapping.

Measure. Yes-rate per arm = "That's me" taps ÷ all taps. No-tap is excluded from both arms and reported.

Pass rule. True yes-rate minus shuffled yes-rate ≥ 10 percentage points, and two-proportion z-test, two-sided, p < 0.05. Both conditions required.

Readability and power. ≥100 taps per arm to publish rates. At 100 per arm a true 10-point gap is detected roughly one time in three, so a non-pass below 385 per arm is published as "not yet decisive", with both rates and both n. Fail is declared only at ≥385 per arm with both conditions unmet.

A pass means. The reflection carries something specific to the person beyond what any warm sentence carries. It does not mean the reflection is true, and never cause.

On a fail. The front-page line comes down the day a fail is declared. The page says "flattery wearing a truth's clothes", with both rates and both n.

Read date. 9 Nov 2026 publishes the state of this test: build live or not, taps per arm to date, and "not enough people yet". The read repeats every Monday until readable.

C1 (5 Nov 2026): the fear-to-anger transition — a count, not a test

Question. Of people whose first named state is Fear, what share name Anger next within 14 days?

Population and window. Every person whose first state-naming is Fear between 25 May 2026 and 15 Nov 2026, all markets. The 14-day follow-up closes 29 Nov 2026.

Definition. Fear→Anger: first named state is Fear and the next named state, at any session within 14 days, is Anger. Fear→Other: next named state within 14 days is anything else. Denominator: all people with first state Fear who name a second state within 14 days. Numerator: Fear→Anger. People with first state Fear who never name again within 14 days are excluded from the denominator and reported as a separate count.

What is published. Two shares, each with a 95% Wilson interval and n: (i) the conditional share, Fear→Anger ÷ people who named a second state within 14 days; (ii) the unconditional share, Fear→Anger ÷ all first-Fear people, with the never-named-again count visible beside it. As frozen context, the same two shares over a 30-day window; the same next-state share for every other first state, as context; weekly bins by date of first naming where a bin has ≥15 people.

Pass rule. None. We have never counted this transition and hold no base rate, so no honest directional expectation exists yet. Registering one would be a guess.

Readability. ≥30 people in the conditional denominator. The Fear and Anger word lists are frozen and fingerprinted in this registration (see Word lists). If not met: "not enough people yet."

What it means. A description of our own data. Never cause. Any directional hypothesis about this transition (for example, that the share rises around external escalations) will be registered as a separate entry, before further data is read, or not at all.

Read date. 30 Nov 2026.

WHICH IS WHICH
H4, H5, H6 and H7 are hypothesis tests with a pre-stated pass and fail. C1 is a descriptive count with a pre-stated denominator and no pass/fail.

FINGERPRINTS AND CANONICAL TEXT
The SHA-256 fingerprints quoted in H4, H5 and H6 were computed over the text blocks as published on satya.org/research, satya.org/research-awareness and satya.org/research-dimensions on 17–18 Oct 2026. Those pages are the canonical text. The quotations here are re-typed and differ in punctuation; hashing this document will not reproduce those fingerprints. To verify, hash the site's block. H4, H5 and H6 are being registered on OSF only now, 5 Nov 2026, after their first reads were scheduled (30 Nov 2026) but before any read is published. H7 and C1 are written and submitted for the first time today, after the 31 Oct 2026 wire release promised them publicly and before either read date.

Contact: info@satya.org · Abhishek Kumar Raysingh, Raydyn, Inc.

report: Reporting *p* values imprecisely (e.g., *p* < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in *p* value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list("P-Value" = c("p < 0.05", "p < 0.05", "p < 0.05", 
"p < 0.05"), Text = c("Pass if Spearman ρ ≥ 0.30 (two-sided p < 0.05, 10,000 permutations); secondary, Peace ρ ≤ -0.30.", 
"Fisher exact, two-sided, p < 0.05.", "True yes-rate minus shuffled yes-rate ≥ 10 percentage points, and two-proportion z-test, two-sided, p < 0.05.", 
"Fisher exact, twosided, p < 0.05; readable only with at least 60 named and 200 not named."
)), row.names = c(NA, -4L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"
))

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 2, FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} The APA manual states: Report exact *p* values (e.g., *p* = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report *p* values less than .001 as *p* < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a *p* value meta-analysis), so report *p* values with three digits. American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association. :::

#### README Files

README files are a way to document the contents and structure of a folder, helping users locate the information they need. You can use a README to document changes to a repository, and explain how files are named. Please consider adding a README to each repository or including 'README' in the name of your overview document.

#### Registration's Source Project Is Closed

1 OSF source project is closed. The files metacheck lists below were not read from it — they were retrieved from the OSF registration's own copy, which is separate from and unaffected by the project's access setting. Nothing is currently lost, but this is still worth fixing: a closed source project means the files only survive for as long as the registration's copy does, and anyone who follows the project link itself (rather than the registration) will find it inaccessible.

- **https://osf.io/jexdh** is closed; its files were retrieved from the OSF registration https://osf.io/krs8a, osf.io/krs8a.

info.title: Pre-registered protocol: Felt Intelligence reads scored by the person. Hypotheses H4 to H7, count C1, frozen lexicon and scoring rules. No results reported

text.text: This is a pre-registration, not a result.

It records, before any scoring, the tests a small research project will run on Felt Intelligence (FI), a reading of a person that the person scores: a dated line about their own past is spoken, they answer "That's me" or "Not quite", and their answer outranks the reading.
Four hypothesis tests (H4, H5, H6, H7) and one descriptive count (C1) are stated with their populations, windows, measures, pass rules, readability thresholds and fail actions.
H4 to H6 were first published on satya.org on 17 and 18 October 2026 with SHA-256 fingerprints; H7 and C1 were written on 5 November 2026.
The identical text was registered on the Open Science Framework on 5 November 2026 at 10:41 UTC (osf.io/krs8a).
H7 is unrun; its window opens only when the shuffled-delivery build is live, and that date will be published before any tap counts.
The window label on the first-reflection count (529) is being settled and logged before a single claim is scored.
No outcome is promised.
Nothing here is called proven.
Reads are published pass, fail, not yet decisive, or "not enough people yet", with denominators, at satya.org/research.
Satya -Felt Intelligence: pre-registered reads Raydyn, Inc., a Delaware public benefit corporation • satya.org • submitted for OSF registration 5 Nov 2026
Satya is an attention-continuity interface built on Felt Intelligence (FI).
A person hears one dated line about their own past -the first reflection -and answers "That's me" or "Not quite"; their answer outranks the reading.
Every count is published at satya.org/research with its date and denominator, misses beside hits.
No outcome is promised; nothing here is called proven.
Not wellness, not therapy.
count, and the number of excluded rows is published with each read.
-No person's words are reproduced in any publication.
-Who reads: one named person, Abhishek Kumar Raysingh, read-only, and no read before the read date.
Each read publishes the analysis file used and its SHA-256; analysis files are frozen in this OSF project before the read they serve.
-Word lists: the word-to-rung lexicon of the tap path is frozen in this project as word_rung_lexicon_2026-11-05.txt, SHA-256 3414eb3116fcb953538cf9686be061c99efdc5903cce19c66dac0de27ccc804e.
The transcript grader's state word lists are a second list; their fingerprint is added to this project before the first read that uses them (30 Nov 2026).
-Every read is published pass, fail, not yet decisive, or "not enough people yet", with both rates and both n, at satya.org/research.

H4 • written 17 Oct 2026 before the data (satya.org/research): across weekly bins 25 May → 29 Nov 2026, does the weekly share of our people's state-namings below the Witness co-move with the weekly English-Wikipedia War share?
Pass if Spearman ρ ≥ 0.30 (two-sided p < 0.05, 10,000 permutations); secondary, Peace ρ ≤ -0.30.
text.formatted: Pass if Spearman ρ ≥ 0.30 (two-sided p < 0.05, 10,000 permutations); secondary, Peace ρ ≤ -0.30.

text.text: Readable only if at least 25 weeks each have at least 15 namings.
At the pace as of 17 Oct 2026 -about 6 namings a weekthe 30 Nov read will probably say not enough people yet; it will be published as that.
A pass is moving together, never cause.
Whether a rise inside moves the outside is deferred until 10,000 members name a state.

Fingerprint of the written test (SHA-256): c177e7defcd464624071bb2f357531f7095967a453b6659b7c9618874ad652d9 H5 • written 18 Oct 2026, before the data (satya.org/research-awareness): Does the pause mean anything?

Among people whose first "That's me" is timed, do those who answered after 8 seconds or more come back for another session within 14 days at a rate at least 10 points higher than those who answered in under 2 seconds?
Fisher exact, two-sided, p < 0.05.
Readable only with at least 150 people and at least 30 in the fast group -as of 18 Oct 2026, 28 fast taps of 191 timed first taps the 30 Nov read will probably say "not enough people yet".
A pass would be comovement, never cause.
The clock is unchanged: it still includes hearing the truth.
Fingerprint (SHA-256): c3ca7163b0d4c428582ef7e44f2e41a3a7dc9e28676f51cec2138126bacb6adc Question.
Does a person say "That's me" to their own first reflection more often than to a first reflection written for a stranger?
Window.
Opens at the first 00:00 UTC after the shuffled-delivery build is live in all three markets (US, UK, India).
That date is published at satya.org/research before the first tap counts.
The window stays open until readability is met.
Consent.
Before the tap every person sees: "The line you are about to hear was written either for you or for someone else.
Tell us if it's you.
Your own line follows either way."
The shuffled line carries no name, birth data or place.
A person who declines goes straight to their own reflection, is excluded from both arms, and is counted.
Conditions.
At generation, each person is randomly assigned 1:1.

True read: the first reflection generated for person X is delivered to X. Shuffled read: the first reflection generated for X is delivered, unaltered, to person Y -same market, same language -and Y scores it with the same tap.
Y receives their own reflection immediately after tapping.
Measure.
Yes-rate per arm = "That's me" taps ÷ all taps.
No-tap is excluded from both arms and reported.
Pass rule.
True yes-rate minus shuffled yes-rate ≥ 10 percentage points, and two-proportion z-test, two-sided, p < 0.05.
text.formatted: True yes-rate minus shuffled yes-rate ≥ 10 percentage points, and two-proportion z-test, two-sided, p < 0.05.

text.text: Both conditions required.
Readability and power. ≥100 taps per arm to publish rates.
At 100 per arm a true 10-point gap is detected roughly one time in three, so a non-pass below 385 per arm is published as "not yet decisive", with both rates and both n.
Fail is declared only at ≥385 per arm with both conditions unmet.
A pass means.
The reflection carries something specific to the person beyond what any warm sentence carries.
It does not mean the reflection is true, and never cause.
On a fail.
The front-page line comes down the day a fail is declared.
The page says "flattery wearing a truth's clothes", with both rates and both n.
Read date.
9 Nov 2026 publishes the state of this test: build live or not, taps per arm to date, and "not enough people yet".
The read repeats every Monday until readable.
Definition.
Fear→Anger: first named state is Fear and the next named state, at any session within 14 days, is Anger.
Fear→Other: next named state within 14 days is anything else.
Denominator: all people with first state Fear who name a second state within 14 days.
Numerator: Fear→Anger.
People with first state Fear who never name again within 14 days are excluded from the denominator and reported as a separate count.
What is published.

Two shares, each with a 95% Wilson interval and n: (i) the conditional share, Fear→Anger ÷ people who named a second state within 14 days; (ii) the unconditional share, Fear→Anger ÷ all first-Fear people, with the never-named-again count visible beside it.
As frozen context, the same two shares over a 30-day window; the same next-state share for every other first state, as context; weekly bins by date of first naming where a bin has ≥15 people.
Pass rule.
None.
We have never counted this transition and hold no base rate, so no honest directional expectation exists yet.
Registering one would be a guess.
Readability. ≥30 people in the conditional denominator.
The Fear and Anger word lists are frozen and fingerprinted in this registration (see Word lists).
If not met: "not enough people yet."
What it means.
A description of our own data.
Never cause.
Any directional hypothesis about this transition (for example, that the share rises around external escalations) will be registered as a separate entry, before further data is read, or not at all.
Read date.
H4, H5, H6 and H7 are hypothesis tests with a pre-stated pass and fail.
C1 is a descriptive count with a pre-stated denominator and no pass/fail.

The SHA-256 fingerprints quoted in H4, H5 and H6 were computed over the text blocks as published on satya.org/research, satya.org/research-awareness and satya.org/research-dimensions on 17-18 Oct 2026.
Those pages are the canonical text.
The quotations here are re-typed and differ in punctuation; hashing this document will not reproduce those fingerprints.
To verify, hash the site's block.
H4, H5 and H6 are being registered on OSF only now, 5 Nov 2026, after their first reads were scheduled (30 Nov 2026) but before any read is published.
H7 and C1 are written and submitted for the first time today, after the 31 Oct 2026 wire release promised them publicly and before either read date.
